mythology: In the Alopibagh tradition, a part of Sati's hand fell here and vanished. Devotees worship Alopi Shankari in the form of a covered wooden cradle above the sacred kund.
pilgrimage_significance: One of Prayagraj's Shakta pilgrimage sites. The eighteen-peetha stotram names Madhaveswari at Prayaga. This scene follows the Alopibagh tradition.
historical_notes: The bilingual street arch names the Shakti Peetha in Hindi and Tamil. Prayagraj district records a figurative Shiva image and a Shiva lingam at Alopi and lists Lalita Devi separately at Mirapur.
